title: Differentiation of Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
summary: d/dx eˣ = eˣ; d/dx aˣ = aˣ log a; d/dx log x = 1/x (x > 0). With the chain rule: d/dx e^(f(x)) = e^(f(x)) f'(x) and d/dx log f(x) = f'(x)/f(x). For example d/dx log(2x + 3) = 2/(2x + 3).
Simplify first: e^(−3 log x) = x⁻³, so its derivative is −3x⁻⁴.
For y = u^v (variable base and power), take logs: log y = v log u, then differentiate: (1/y) dy/dx = v' log u + v u'/u. Example: d/dx(xˣ) = xˣ(1 + log x).
For y = Ae^(kx) + Be^(−kx), y'' = k²y. Example: y = 500e^(7x) + 600e^(−7x) gives y'' = 49y.
Derivative of sin x with respect to log x = (cos x)/(1/x) = x cos x.

If y = e^(−3 log x), then dy/dx is —

mcq.work: e^(−3 log x) = e^(log x⁻³) = x⁻³ ⇒ dy/dx = −3x⁻⁴.

mcq: The derivative of sin x with respect to log x is —

mcq.work: (d sin x/dx)/(d log x/dx) = cos x/(1/x) = x cos x.

objective: Fill in the blanks: (a) If y = e^(sin⁻¹x), then dy/dx = ______. (b) d/dx(xˣ) = ______.

(a) e^(sin⁻¹x) × 1/√(1 − x²).
(b) log y = x log x ⇒ y'/y = log x + 1 ⇒ xˣ(1 + log x).
True or False: (a) If y = 500e^(7x) + 600e^(−7x), then d²y/dx² = 49y. (b) d/dx(log x²) = 1/x².

(a) True: y' = 3500e^(7x) − 4200e^(−7x), y'' = 24500e^(7x) + 29400e^(−7x) = 49y.
(b) False — log x² = 2 log x, derivative 2/x.
vsa: If y = eˣ log(1 + x²), find dy/dx.
Product rule: eˣ log(1 + x²) + eˣ × 2x/(1 + x²) = eˣ[log(1 + x²) + 2x/(1 + x²)].
Find dy/dx for y = x^(x cos x).

log y = x cos x log x.
(1/y)y' = cos x log x − x sin x log x + cos x.
y' = x^(x cos x)[cos x(1 + log x) − x sin x log x].
sa: If x = a(cos θ + log tan(θ/2)) and y = a sin θ, find d²y/dx².

dx/dθ = a(−sin θ + 1/sin θ) = a cos²θ/sin θ. dy/dθ = a cos θ.
dy/dx = a cos θ × sin θ/(a cos²θ) = tan θ.
d²y/dx² = sec²θ × dθ/dx = sec²θ × sin θ/(a cos²θ) = sin θ/(a cos⁴θ).
